title: Bhrigu and the layers of a person
hook: a son asks his father what is ultimately real, and finds a person has layers
carry: the subtle body: more of you than flesh
tomorrow: the old map starts with someone asleep at the bottom. who?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Jagannath's unfinished wood and a yantra on an altar, and prana pratishtha: the presence is invited, not bought. Today the map moves into the body, and a young man goes looking for what's real.

In the Taittiriya Upanishad, a young man named Bhrigu goes to his father, the god Varuna, and asks: teach me Brahman, the ultimate reality. Varuna doesn't lecture. He points: food, breath, sight, hearing, mind, speech. Then he says: that from which beings are born, by which they live, into which they return, seek that. Seek it through tapas, steady disciplined effort. Go and practice. Bhrigu goes off, works at it, and comes back sure. It's food; everything is made of it. Go again, says his father.
screen: `TEACH ME BRAHMAN.` → `HE POINTS: SEEK THAT.` → `IT'S FOOD. GO AGAIN.`

segments.voice: So he goes again. Breath, he decides next, the life that moves the body. Go again. Then mind. Then understanding. And at last, joy, ananda, and this time he isn't sent back. The same Upanishad describes a person in five koshas, sheaths, each finer than the last: the body made of food, then breath, mind, understanding and bliss. Vedanta groups the middle three into the sukshma sharira, the subtle body: a real part of you that isn't made of flesh. That's the big teaching: you are more than the body you can weigh. And it's where the chakras live. Chakra means a wheel or a circle, and the yoga texts place them in the subtle body, along the spine, pictured as lotuses. Now the modern argument: no scan has ever found one. Inside the tradition there are two answers, and each deserves its best case. One view: of course not. A scanner sees the body made of food, Bhrigu's first answer, and the subtle body was never said to be tissue. Another view, held by many teachers: the chakras are a map for meditation, telling you where to rest attention, and a map is tested by walking it. Notice what both agree on. Neither calls the chakras organs. Bhrigu's first answer wasn't wrong. It was only the first layer.
screen: `BREATH. MIND. UNDERSTANDING. JOY.` · `KOSHAS AND THE SUBTLE BODY.` · `CHAKRAS: WHEELS IN THE SUBTLE BODY.` · `NO SCAN FINDS THEM: TWO ANSWERS.` · then, large: `MORE OF YOU THAN FLESH.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and climb Bhrigu's layers. Feel the body's weight on the seat. Then the breath moving. Then thoughts passing. Then notice the one who's noticing all of it, and rest there. If you pray, you can offer that stillness; if not, simply stay with it.
The chakras as a map: centers along the spine, pictured as lotuses, placed by the tradition in the subtle body, not in tissue.
screen: `THE CHAKRAS AS A MAP — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the subtle body, more of you than flesh. Bhrigu kept going past the first layer. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu teaching describes a person in five sheaths (koshas), and Vedanta speaks of a gross, a subtle and a causal body; the chakras are placed in the subtle body and taught inside meditation, usually with a teacher. Some teachers stress the subtle body as real, others the chakras as a sequence for placing attention.

Confirm that the subtle-body framing (sukshma sharira; not tissue, known in practice) is a fair statement of how traditional teachers hold the chakras, and that 'neither calls the chakras organs' is fair to both.
